reasons.realCost: ActiveCampaign's published contact-tier price is the annual-billing rate a buyer actually pays, and every plan bundles automation and CRM with no required add-on, but the public pricing page never states the monthly (non-annual) rate that its own billing help article confirms exists.
reasons.pricingHonesty: ActiveCampaign publishes detailed contact-tier pricing across all four plans, but hides the monthly-cadence rate, extra-seat prices, and every CRM and SMS add-on price behind a login rather than the public site.
reasons.smallTeamFit: ActiveCampaign offers a 14-day no-card trial and includes a free onboarding session or AI course on every paid plan, though its automation-and-CRM feature set is broader than a simple newsletter tool and needs more setup time to use fully.
reasons.doesTheJob: Every ActiveCampaign plan, including the cheapest Starter tier, bundles marketing automation with a built-in CRM, letting a small business skip a separate CRM subscription.
reasons.freedomToLeave: ActiveCampaign offers a 30-day money-back guarantee and archives rather than deletes account data for a year after cancellation, but its pricing page shows only annual billing with no visible monthly toggle, nudging buyers toward a longer commitment.
reasons.trackRecord: ActiveCampaign has operated since 2003 and ran without outside funding until 2016.

basis: ActiveCampaign is a solid buy for a small business that wants automation and light CRM in one subscription from a stable, long-run company, though its pricing page hides the monthly-billing rate and every add-on price, and its automation depth asks more setup time than a simpler newsletter tool.
method: Two independent blind passes scored six factors (1–5) and an overall; published overall is the mean of the two overall scores, rounded down. Pass scores: 3.9 and 3.4.
